A.trend: Traced research series with its window. It quantifies the change (CAGR 36.6%, late/early ratio 6.19) and reads the news series separately. The censoring note is carried but 2025 is not visibly marked.
A.comparison: Main pull vs counter pull on one scale, with tier weights defined. Correctly flags that the counter pull is asymmetric by design.
A.chart: One fully traced chart, but it shows volume only. The stance tally, which bears directly on the question, is not charted.
A.drilldown: Orientation, contribution and documents carry Prism ids and DOIs. Only 2 of 7 follow-ups executed; at ceiling.
A.export: Two traced CSVs with provenance JSON. No documents/DOI table.
A.repro: 38/38 numbers traced, full prism-calls block. Memory background is explicitly labelled and not relied on.
A.refs: All 11 DOIs resolve, quotes are verbatim, tier is stated, and the rejected 13-22% figure is flagged. No contrary-side sources exist to tier.
A.accuracy: Catches the anomalies: the 755 'supporting' count is a framing label, and the 13-22% extraction was rejected. The 'reachability checks' line is not in the record.
A.limits: Gap to today, censoring, lane breadth, self-report and pandemic sampling are placed near the numbers. It says what it cannot answer.
A.verdict: Direct answer with decision, low confidence with reason, and change condition. Notes that RCTs are absent from the pull.

B.trend: Chart of study years labelled estimate.
B.refs: The Gibbs DOI/venue is not found, which caps refs at 1. The Emanuel-Harrington reference has no identifier.
B.accuracy: Gibbs et al. is misattributed to Management Science 2024 (it is JPE Micro). The chart puts Bloom in 2013 while the CSV says 2015.
B.limits: Specific about what is unmeasured, but no data limits are possible.
B.verdict: Reasonable 'it varies' answer with decision, confidence and change condition. Supported only by memory studies with venue errors.

C.trend: Traced series with exact delta (+621, 12.1x) and censoring noted. No CAGR is given.
C.comparison: 0 vs 5 on the targeted-read baseline, defined, with a not-representative caveat. Omits the counter-pull design bias.
C.export: Single traced CSV with provenance JSON; no documents table.
C.repro: Fully traced. The 'research window ends 1 year ago' is imprecise (~10 months).
C.refs: 3 DOIs resolve, quotes are verbatim and tiers are given.
C.accuracy: The verdict says targeted reads 'found papers on both sides', but no read paper supported the claim. This contradicts its own data.
C.limits: Lane, windows, gap and censoring are stated, and it declines to use the rejected figure.
C.verdict: The decision, confidence and change condition are present. The 'both sides' framing is inconsistent with the deliverable's evidence.
C.facets: Corpus facets are covered; the RCT vs pandemic tension is barely addressed.

D.trend: Cross-study effect sizes are plotted as a 'trend', labelled estimate.
D.comparison: Memory numbers across non-comparable baselines; the mismatch is acknowledged.
D.drilldown: Generic memory layers. Some follow-ups ran, but no traced layer.
D.refs: 3/7 have DOIs, which resolve. Others lack identifiers, and no quotes are given.
D.accuracy: Attributes an 8-19% output fall to Yang et al. (a collaboration study). It appears to have swapped figures with Gibbs et al. (productivity fell 8-19%, hours up ~30%).
D.limits: Honest about memory, selection and window, but no data limits are possible.
D.verdict: Addresses hybrid RCTs vs fully remote directly, with decision and confidence. Rests partly on misattributed numbers.

A: 'All tables passed reachability checks' is not supported by the reference record
B: Gibbs, Mengel, Siemroth is cited as Management Science 2024 with an unresolvable DOI; it was published in JPE Microeconomics 2023
Bloom et al. is dated 2013 in the chart but 2015 elsewhere
C: The verdict claims papers 'on both sides', but the targeted reads found 0 supporting
'Research window ends 1 year ago' overstates the ~10-month gap
D: Yang et al. (Nature Human Behaviour 2022) is credited with an 8-19% output fall; that study measured collaboration, and the 8-19% figure belongs to Gibbs et al.
The Gibbs et al. 'output per hour fell about 20%' figure is misstated
A line chart joins non-comparable studies as a trend

raw.verdict: A was the only deliverable that read its own data honestly. It surfaced that zero read papers supported the claim and flagged the rejected 13-22% statistic and the framing-label trap. It also gave a low-confidence verdict noting that RCTs were absent from the pull. C used the same data but misstated it as 'both sides' and had no working follow-ups. B and D carried the substantive RCT-vs-pandemic content from memory, but with misattributed venues and effect sizes.
